rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rahman is a divine attribute exclusive to God whose relation is not a particular act; its primordial grace extends universally without condition.
rows.anchor: Rahmâniyetin Allah’a ihtisâsı ve mâ‘adâya ta‘alluk-ı fi‘lî ifade etmeyip ancak bi’l-izâfe âmil olması ekvânda bilâ-şart-ı şey’ bir umum ifade eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every creature's original gifts and existence arise from Rahman's grace, received without anyone's earned choice.
rows.anchor: Her şeyin ilk halk ve îcâdında almış olduğu bütün mevâhib-i fıtriye rahmâniyetin izâfeti eseridir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Primordial creation is compelled and bestowed: stones, trees, and humans have their kinds through this unchosen mercy.
rows.anchor: Taşın taş, ağacın ağaç, insanın insan olması böyle bir rahmet-i cebriyenin eseridir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All realms and beings, from obedient and believing to rebellious and idolatrous, are immersed in Rahman's mercy and freed from fear in that respect.
rows.anchor: âlemlerin hepsi rahmet-i Rahmân’a müstağraktır ve bu haysiyetle mehâfetten âzâdedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If this universal grace were all, distinctions between knowledge and ignorance, life and death, effort and idleness, obedience and disobedience, and faith and unbelief would disappear.
rows.anchor: Lâkin bu kadarla kalsa idi, ilim ile cehlin, hayât ile mevtin, sa‘y ile atâletin, itaat ile isyanın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without a further mercy enabling agency, people would be determinists and compelled beings, unable to act on what they know or desire.
rows.anchor: hep tabîî olurduk, tabi‘iyyûndan, cebriyyûndan olurduk

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's wisdom requires that He display His own will and create creatures who possess will, rather than make all action compulsory.
rows.anchor: Cenâb-ı Allah’ın kendi irade ve ihtiyârını göstermesi ve onun eseri olarak sâhib-i irâde mahlûkāt halk etmesi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God advances creatures according to good choices and grants enjoyment of mercy, while bad choices bring deprivation, pain, and punishment; this harmonizes their wills with His.
rows.anchor: hüsn-i irade ve ihtiyarlarına göre terakki ettirerek rahmetinden mütena‘‘im ve müstefid ve bilakis sû’-i irade ve kesblerine göre mahrûmiyetle, elem ve ‘ikāb ile mu‘âteb

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rahman is the instinctive grace seen in mother birds beating their wings over their young.
rows.anchor: Ana kuşlar eser-i rahmâniyet olan sevk-i fıtrî ile yavrularının başında kanat çırpar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rahim is the grace through which ethical people compete in compassion and good works.
rows.anchor: ahlâklı insanlar da eser-i rahîmiyetle vücûh-ı hayr üzerinde rahm u şefkatle müsâbaka ederler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rahman's first mercy brings everyone into existence and sustains them regardless of effort.
rows.anchor: İbtidâ çalışana çalışmayana bakmadan vücûda sevk ve o suretle idare etmek bir rahmet-i rahmâniyedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rahim's further mercy grants the goals achieved by those who work.
rows.anchor: Bilâhare çalışanlara çalıştıkları gayeleri de ayrıca bahş etmek bir rahmet-i rahîmiyedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rahman gives absolute hope and prevents universal despair; without it humans would lack existence and essential natural gifts.
rows.anchor: Rahmâniyet ye’s-i mutlaka, umûmî bedbinliğe imkân bırakmayan bir ümîd-i mutlak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rahim answers particular despair, sustains specific aims and effort, and rewards responsibility.
rows.anchor: Rahîmiyet ise ye’s-i hâssın cevâbı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Under Rahman's universal grace believers and unbelievers, and this world and the next, are equal; Rahim's grace sharply distinguishes them, as the two groups in 42:7 show.
rows.anchor: rahmâniyetin karşısında dünya ve âhiret, mü’min ve kâfir müsâvî iken rahîmiyetin karşısında bunlar bir fark-ı bâriz ile ayrılıyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thus the inherited formulations call God Rahman of this world and the next but Rahim of the next, or Rahman of believer and unbeliever but Rahim of the believer.
rows.anchor: “dünya ve âhiretin Rahmân’ı ve âhiretin Rahîm’i” yahut “mü’min ve kâfirin Rahmân’ı, mü’minin Rahîm’i”

rows.speaker: Şeyh Abduh
rows.claim: Abduh neglects the inherited distinction because he assumes the lexicon does not support it; Elmalılı says this is mistaken.
rows.anchor: Şeyh Abduh merhûmun lügatta bunlara işaret yoktur zannıyla eslâfın bu tâbirlerle gösterdikleri farkları ihmâl etmesi doğru değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lexically Rahman is a predominant attribute specific to God, without an active relation and suggestive of eternity and the beginning; Rahim has an active relation and continues without end.
rows.anchor: gālibedendir ve ta‘alluk-i fi‘lîsi yoktur. Ezeliyeti müş‘ir ve mebde’e nâzırdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rahman's mercy is an essential attribute of willing good at the outset, while Rahim's is an active attribute of doing good at the end.
rows.anchor: Rahmet-i Rahmân, ibtidâen irâde-i hayra râci‘bir sıfat-ı zâtiye

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rahman and Rahim are not repeated merely for emphasis: each has its own foundational meaning and distinct mode of intensification.
rows.anchor: “Rahmân” ile “Rahîm” başka başka birer ma‘nâ-yı rahmeti hâiz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rahman is more emphatic in encompassing every creature, while Rahim is more emphatic in actual beneficence, which also operates through servants.
rows.anchor: Bir cihetten rahmet-i Rahmân eblağdır, çünkü her mahlûka muzâf olur. Diğer cihetten rahmet-i Rahîm eblağdır

rows.speaker: Bazı tefsirler
rows.claim: Some commentaries associate Rahman's mercy with great blessings and Rahim's with the subtleties of blessings.
rows.anchor: Bazı tefsirlerde de buna işâreten “rahmet-i Rahmân celâil-i ni‘am, rahmet-i Rahîm ise dekāik-i ni‘am ile alâkadardır” derler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The grammatical pattern distinguishes them: Rahman's subject is restricted while its object is general; Rahim's subject is general while its object is restricted.
rows.anchor: “Rahmân”ın mevsûfu hâs, müte‘allakı âmdır. “Rahîm”in mevsûfu âm, müte‘allakı hâstır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Together these attributes replace pessimism with boundless optimism, the spirit of faith; the first benefit received from the basmala is this hope, affirmed by 28:83.
rows.anchor: Rahmân-ı Rahîm’i münkir olan kâfir istediği kadar bedbin olsun, fakat mü’minin bedbinliğine hiçbir sebep yoktur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala has an apparent structure of one genitive relation, two adjectival relations, and an initial attachment; its hidden relation makes it a complete, concise statement.
rows.anchor: Besmele zâhirde bir nisbet-i izâfiye ile iki nisbet-i vasfiyye ve başında bir nisbet-i ta‘alluktan mürekkeb

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ism Allah may be read as a genitive meaning either Allah's name or the name Allah.
rows.anchor: beyâniye olabilir ki evvelkinde “Allah’ın ismi”, ikincide “Allah ismi” demek olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the lamiyya reading the adjectives can be construed before or after the genitive; on the bayaniyya reading the whole epitheted name is cited as one name and then explains ism.
rows.anchor: “Rahmân ve Rahîm sıfatlarıyla muttasıf bulunan Cenâb-ı Allah’ın ismiyle”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bayaniyya analysis treats the genitive inflection as distributed over three words to stress the divine proper name, a necessary inflection rather than ordinary narration grammar.
rows.anchor: ki buna “i‘râb-ı zarûrî” nâmı verilir

rows.speaker: Müfessirînin çoğu
rows.claim: Most commentators prefer the lamiyya construction because its parsing is explicit and the meanings of the names and attributes are directly intended.
rows.anchor: Müfessirînin çoğu evvelkini tercih ediyorlar. Çünkü onda hem i‘râb zâhir ve hem esmâ ve sıfâtın mânası bizzat maksud olur

rows.speaker: Bazıları
rows.claim: Some prefer the bayaniyya construction, citing Labid's line using ism al-salam; the Mevlid author also reflects it with Allah adı.
rows.anchor: Bazıları ise Lebîd’in السَّلَاَمِ عَلَيْكُمَا إِلَى الْحَوْلِ ثُمَّ اسْمُ mısrâ‘ındaki اِسْمُ السَّلَاَمِ gibi beyâniyeyi tercih etmişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted verb is the action the speaker is about to undertake, such as reading, writing, eating, or beginning, and the opening ba attaches the name to it.
rows.anchor: fiil besmele diyen kimsenin teşebbüs edeceği

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb and subject are omitted to let anyone connect the basmala to any intended act; ba and the speaker's situation identify the ellipsis, as in Turkish formulas like devletle selâmetle.
rows.anchor: cümlenin erkânı olan fiil ve fâil hazf edilmişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Arabic normally delays a complement, placing the ba phrase first gives emphasis and exclusivity; compared with 96:1, basmala foregrounds Allah's name rather than the act of reading.
rows.anchor: böyle hakkı muahhar olan tetimmenin takdîmi bir ihtimam ve ihtisas ifade eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This fronting makes the beginning exclusive to Allah's name, rejecting the pagan practice of starting with Lat or Uzza and expressing tawhid.
rows.anchor: Arap müşrikleri de sözlerine veya işlerine بِاسْمِ اللَاَّتِ بِاسْمِ الْعُزَّی gibi putlarından birinin ismiyle başlarlardı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turkish word order cannot readily preserve the Arabic exclusivity and the direct joining of the spoken formula to the act; an implied construction can show tawhid but is awkward and loses concision.
rows.anchor: Bunda ise fi‘l-i kavlînin, fi‘l-i hakīkīye mukāreneti temin edilmemiş olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He proposes eight possible Turkish renderings, using both lamiyya and bayaniyya forms such as Allah's name with the two attributes or Allah, Rahman, Rahim as one name.
rows.anchor: 7. Allâh-ı Rahmân-i Rahîm ismiyle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Combining Allah with Rahman and Rahim as one name foregrounds Allah but still fails to connect the act directly with mercy.
rows.anchor: doğrudan doğru Allah ismi mebde’ yapılmış olacak ve ma‘amâfîh vasl-ı rahmet yine temin edilemeyecektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Removing the participle still leaves Allah's proper name insufficiently foregrounded and separates it from the mercy attributes; listing three names may imply three divine essences, though singular ismiyle helps avert that implication.
rows.anchor: “ismiyle” denilip, “isimleriyle” denilmemesi bu îhâmı def‘e kâfi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala's words, composition, rhetoric, sound, and even its sweet pattern of letters cannot be fully carried into Turkish, so it should be recited in Arabic and understood through explanation.
rows.anchor: ne müfredâtını ve ne terkiblerini tamamen terceme mümkin olmayan ve hele vücûh-ı belâgati, âheng-i beyânı hiçbir suretle kābil-i nakl olmayan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects corrupting the tawhid key with a rendering like esirgeciyi bağışlayıcı tanrı adıyla.
rows.anchor: bir miftâh-ı kül ve bir âyet-i tevhîd olan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala's interpretive pivot is ba, which connects Allah's name, the first source and ultimate object of existence and progress, to the intended act.
rows.anchor: olan nokta baştaki با harfidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human acts are not their own complete cause: will is a moment in the stream of existence, and success depends on the outpouring between the First Cause and human will, first Rahmani and finally Rahimi.
rows.anchor: muvaffakiyetlerimiz, illet-i ûlâ ile iradelerimiz arasındaki nisbetin feyzine tâbi‘dir ki bu feyz ibtidâen Rahmânî, intihâen Rahîmîdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala's ba makes this universal relation conscious; its secret is said to lie in the ba's dot, and Hâkânî's poem links the basmala's continuity to the existence of things.
rows.anchor: Olmasa besmele resmi memdûd Cins-i eşyâda olur muydu vücûd

rows.speaker: E‘âzım-ı müfessirîn
rows.claim: The great commentators say ba here means either attachment and accompaniment or seeking aid; the former makes the basmala circumstantial, the latter an indirect object.
rows.anchor: E‘âzım-ı müfessirîn diyorlar ki: “Bâ”nın buradaki ma‘nâ-yı ilsâkı

rows.speaker: Şeyh Abduh
rows.claim: Abduh says customary in the name of means acting for an authority, by its command and on its behalf; the Muslim's basmala can express beginning an act for Allah and by His command.
rows.anchor: Şeyh Abduh merhum Fâtiha tefsîrinde zikre şâyan bir mâna daha kaydetmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says Abduh's deputyship reading amounts to acting as God's representative and self-effacement, appropriate only to special stations such as prophethood, sainthood, rule, and authority.
rows.anchor: ancak risalet, velâyet, hâkimiyet, tasarruf gibi makāmât-ı mahsûsada cârî olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That meaning cannot apply generally: saying one eats in God's name is improper, though saying one eats food God bestowed would be sound; worship is for God but not done as His deputy.
rows.anchor: Çünkü ibadet Allah’a olursa da Allah nâmına niyâbeten değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports that the basmala is the key to every book and every important act imply a general meaning for lawful acts; one of the commentators' attachment or seeking-aid senses supplies it.
rows.anchor: bize besmelenin meşrû olan her işimizin küşâdında miftah olabilecek bir ma‘nâ-yı şâmilini ihtar etmektedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abduh's explanation is sound for the Quran's revelation, recitation, and writing because of the basmala's position at their beginnings, and it matters in special settings too.
rows.anchor: Kur’ân’ın, süver-i Kur’ân’ın nüzûlü, kıraati, kitabeti itibariyle evvelinde bulunması haysiyetinden besmelenin mânasında Şeyh Abduh’un îzâhı doğru olduğu gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stopping after only bism is defective; stopping after Bismillah or after Rahman is sufficient and sound, and the complete stop follows Rahim.
rows.anchor: Besmele derken بِسْمِ üzerinde durmak nâkıs ve kabih, بِسْمِ اللّٰهِ deyip durmak kâfi ve sahih

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When writing a mushaf, writing the basmala at each surah opening except Bara'a is obligatory.
rows.anchor: Mushaf yazarken Berâe’den mâ‘adâ sûre başlarında بِسْمِ اللّٰهِ الرَّحْمٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ yazmak farzdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For slaughter or shooting game, saying Bismillah alone is obligatory; deliberate omission makes the animal unlawful, but forgetfulness is excused.
rows.anchor: Hayvan zebh ederken veya ava silah atarken sadece بسم اللّٰه demek de farzdır. Kasden terk edilirse o hayvan yenmez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In slaughter and similar settings, omitting Rahman and Rahim is sunnah.
rows.anchor: Bunda ve bu gibi bazı mevâki‘de الرَّحْمٰن الرَّحِيم denilmemek sünnettir

rows.speaker: Cumhûr
rows.claim: Outside prayer, beginning a surah recitation with isti'adha and basmala is sunnah according to the majority, while some imams such as Ata consider it obligatory.
rows.anchor: demek cumhûra göre sünnet, ezcümle Atâ gibi bazı e’immeye göre vâcibdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no basmala at Bara'a's opening; in the Asim reading, reciting it between two surahs is recommended, and starting midway or at the end also recommends isti'adha and basmala.
rows.anchor: Yalnız Berâe’de besmele denmez. Sûreteyn beyninde iki kıraat vardır. Bizim Âsım kıraatinde okumak mendubdur

rows.speaker: Hanefîler
rows.claim: In prayer before al-Fatiha, Hanafis recommend silently reciting isti'adha and basmala.
rows.anchor: namazda biz Hanefîlere göre Fâtiha’dan evvel sırren eûzü-besmele sünnet

rows.speaker: Şâfiiyye
rows.claim: Shafi'is require basmala in prayer, either silently or aloud.
rows.anchor: Şâfiiyye’ye göre sırren veya cehren besmele farz

rows.speaker: Mâlikîler
rows.claim: Malikis recommend omitting basmala in prayer.
rows.anchor: Mâlikîlere göre okunmaması mendubdur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beginning other important, lawful affairs with Bismillah, with or without Rahman and Rahim, is recommended, sunnah, or obligatory according to circumstances.
rows.anchor: Kıraatten mâ‘adâ sâir umûr-i mühimme ve meşrû‘aya بِسْمِ اللّٰهِ veya بِسْمِ اللّٰهِ الرَّحْمٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ ile başlamak derecâtına göre mendub veya sünnet veya vâcibdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He directs readers to later discussions of isti'adha at 16:98, general naming at al-Alaq, slaughter at al-Anam, and basmala again at al-Naml.
rows.anchor: İsti‘âze meselesi فَإِذَا قَرَأْتَ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ فَٱسْتَعِذْ بِٱللَّهِ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's moral character and mission as mercy to the worlds ground his selection and training; God taught him to begin with the divine name and its exclusive relation.
rows.anchor: evvelemirde onun ıstıfâsına, tehzîb ve te’dîbine ‘inâyet-i rabbâniyesini izhâr

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave the community the basmala as a universal key and made its use at the start of books, writing, recitation, speeches, and needs a prophetic sunnah.
rows.anchor: mebde’-i ümîdi ve müntehâ-yı âmâli olan ‘inâyet-i Rahmâniye ve rahmet-i Rahîmiyeyi

rows.speaker: Resûl-i Ekrem
rows.claim: A prophetic hadith calls the basmala the key to every book.
rows.anchor: Resûl-i Ekrem Efendimiz’in hadîs-i şerîflerinde de şöyle vârid olmuştur: بِسْمِ اللّٰهِ الرَّحْمٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ مِفْتَاحُ كُلِّ كِتَابٍ

rows.speaker: Resûl-i Ekrem
rows.claim: Another prophetic hadith says an important matter not begun with Allah's name is abtar, truncated; without it a work cannot be presented before God and remains deficient.
rows.anchor: Her mühim iş ki bismillah ile başlanmamıştır güdüktür vesselâm

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala summarizes the Quran's subject and aim; al-Fatiha and the successive surahs unfold its inexhaustible detail and wise ordering, beyond merely measurable length or poetic feeling.
rows.anchor: biz bunda ilm-i Kur’ân’ın mevzû‘unu, gayesini icmâlen bulacağız ve evvelâ Fâtiha’da sâniyen peyderpey sûreleriyle bütün Kur’an’da bunun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran is not a chance or merely poetic anthology but a coherent true discourse like a single comprehensive sentence, beginning with basmala and ending with al-Nas.
rows.anchor: Kur’ân’ın sûreleri, âyetleri keyfemettefak bir tesadüfün veya sade bir hiss-i şâirânenin sevkiyle serilivermiş bir dîvân-ı mahlût değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran's whole discourse links Allah to all creatures, especially humans, and their return relation to Him; recitation permutations at completion, transmitted from Ali, are called hal-murtahil and signify no total break in existence.
rows.anchor: ki bu bize vücudda inkıtâ‘-ı tâm olmadığını ifade eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Astronomy studies universal gravitation as one unified subject, yet it does not encompass all existence or even all scientific fields.
rows.anchor: Bugün biliyoruz ki bütün bir ilm-i hey’et bir câzibe kanununun ifadesidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gravity does not cover particle attraction, chemical cohesion, organic nourishment and reproduction, affective attraction and aversion, sensory images, rational truth, spiritual will, or social bonds.
rows.anchor: onda ne ecsâmın zerrâtı veya eczâ-i ferdiyesi arasındaki câzibe-i zerreviye veya cüz’-i ferdiyeyi, temâsük ve telâsuk gibi alâka-i kimyeviyeyi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran's subject unifies every physical and spiritual kind of attraction under absolute lordship and God's relation to the world, especially humanity; gravity is only one partial sign.
rows.anchor: rubûbiyet kanununu, Allah ile âlem ve bilhassa insanlar beynindeki nisbet ve izâfet-i mutlakanın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quranic composition unites scientific order and aesthetic beauty, surpassing the system of sciences in firmness and literature in variety and resemblance.
rows.anchor: Nazm-ı Kur’an nesak-ı ilmî ile nesak-ı bedî‘înin vahdetgâhıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran's integrated order supports its divine origin: if it came from other than God, much inconsistency would be found, as 4:82 says.
rows.anchor: أَفَلَا يَتَدَبَّرُونَ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ وَلَوْ كَانَ مِنْ عِندِ غَيْرِ ٱللَّهِ لَوَجَدُوا۟ فِيهِ ٱخْتِلَٰفًا كَثِيرًا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human science has not measured even the order of the three-body system, so it cannot certify the absence of scientific, logical, or aesthetic flaws in cosmic order.
rows.anchor: yalnız ecsâm-ı selâse nazariyesi dâhilindeki nizam ve nisbetini bile henüz ölçmemiş olan fennimiz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nature's order is both manifest and hidden; the Quran's surah and verse order is similarly, and even more, manifest and hidden, manifest through perfection and hidden through inexhaustibility.
rows.anchor: Fıtratın bu nizâmı, nazarımızda nasıl böyle hem zâhir ve hem bâtın ise, Kur’ân’ın sûreleri ve âyetleri beynindeki nizâm-ı ilmî ve bedî‘î dahi onun gibi ve hatta ondan ziyade zâhir ve ondan ziyade bâtındır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poet says the cosmos' maiden thought has been torn open while the Quran's meaning still remains veiled in its purity.
rows.anchor: Bikr-i fikri kâinâtın çâk çâk oldu fakat Perde-i ‘ismette kaldı ma‘nî-i Kur’ân henüz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People often sacrifice aesthetic relations when thinking logically and logical relations when thinking aesthetically; although they cannot chart all Quranic relations, they can experience their perfection by living it.
rows.anchor: bu tenâsübü bütün kadrosuyla bir cetvel çizer gibi fikren ölçemiyor isek o fıtratı yaşarken bu zevk-i kemâli vecd ile duyabiliriz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To live the universal attraction, readers should seek refuge from distraction and satanic whispering, then take the basmala as key and begin al-Fatiha in gratitude.
rows.anchor: diyelim ve o câzibe-i külliyeyi yaşamak için

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He renders the verse as praise belonging to the Lord of the worlds.
rows.anchor: Meâl: Hamd, o Rabbü’l-âlemîn

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran has an exhaustive, subtle order among surahs, stories, verses, words, and letters; analyzing it involves innumerable sciences, beginning with grammar and rhetoric.
rows.anchor: Kur’an’da sûreler, ekser sûrelerde kıssalar, kıssalarda âyetler, âyetlerde kelimât, kelimâtta hurûf

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quranic rhetoric includes composition, context, implication, modes of expression, logic, wisdom, and the verbal and semantic beauties that secure fluency, force, balance, and inimitability.
rows.anchor: Nazm-ı Kur’an’da terkîb, sibâk, siyâk, mantûk, mefhûm ve fehvâ, mutâbakat, tazammun ve iltizam ile ibâre, işâret, delâlet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These relations combine linguistic convention, rational logic, and natural taste; translation loses much of the first and third and consequently affects logical signification too.
rows.anchor: delâlet-i vaz‘iye ve lisâniye, delâlet-i akliye ve mantıkiye ve delâlet-i tabî‘iye ve zevkiye nâmıyla üç nevi delâletin muhassalası

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because human power cannot detail every relation, he will sketch them in places and pause especially over al-Fatiha.
rows.anchor: Bunun için biz bazı mevâki‘de bu münasebâtı icmâlen göstermeye çalışacağız. Çünkü tafsîline kudret-i beşer kâfi değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Contextual relation may be backward or forward; if the basmala is part of al-Fatiha, backward context is irrelevant, while its relation to 96:1 belongs to revelation order and forward context.
rows.anchor: Besmele Fâtiha’nın bir cüz’ü addolunduğuna göre birincisi mevzu‘-i bahis olamaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nothing lies outside the basmala's attraction, so it relates generally to al-Fatiha as one recites, writes, praises, or begins the Quran in its name.
rows.anchor: Besmele ile Fâtiha okuyorum, Fâtiha yazıyorum, hamd ediyorum, Kur’ân’a başlıyorum ilh… gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Specifically, basmala and al-Fatiha are closely linked by cadence, wording, summary and explanation; al-Fatiha's gratitude answers the basmala's attraction of mercy.
rows.anchor: besmeledeki câzibe-i rahmete Fâtiha’nın bir cevâb-ı şükrân olduğu ilk nazarda görülüyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their structures correspond: the basmala has seven actual or implicit words, four independent words and three divine-name words; al-Fatiha has seven verses, four statements, and three complete pauses, with the middle tawhid verse linking two three-verse units.
rows.anchor: Fâtiha yedi âyet, dört kelâm-ı müstakil, üç vakf-ı tâmdan mürekkeb bir kelâm-ı tâm nizamında bir sûre-i bedî‘adır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala names God and His attributes while leaving humanity implicit; saying it establishes the divine relation that lets al-Fatiha bring humans forth with gratitude into speech.
rows.anchor: Orada اَللّٰه الرَّحْمٰن الرَّحِيم husustan umûma inbisat eden isim ve sıfâtı ile mezkûr iken biz ezelde olduğumuz gibi ef‘âlimizle beraber mahzuf ve muzmer idik

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Fatiha begins in gratitude, places humans in the worlds under a hidden divine relation, renews the manifestation of mercy, and trains consciousness through truth and instruction until people recognize God and themselves.
rows.anchor: Fâtiha bir şükran ile başlıyor ve bizi gıyâbî bir izâfet-i rabbâniye ile

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It then grants people speech to pledge exclusive worship and dependence, binding human will and the right to ask for guidance into an enduring covenant between God and humanity.
rows.anchor: vahdâniyyet-i ilâhiyeye إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ diye bir ‘akd-i bey‘at yaptırmak üzere bize hakk-ı kelâm veriyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hidden humanity of the basmala becomes a speaking subject in al-Fatiha, while God is present as interlocutor; the surah captures the full relation of life and existence.
rows.anchor: ezeldeki ve besmeledeki bâtın, Fâtiha’da ve hâlde bir mütekellim-i zâhir oluyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sacred hadith says al-Fatiha is divided equally between God and servant, with the servant entitled to what is asked; its opening praises and glorifies God, its middle is shared, and its ending is the servant's supplication.
rows.anchor: Ben salât sûresi olan Fâtiha’yı Benim aramla kulum arasında yarı yarıya taksim ettim
